add_decl_unchecked_production_sites.trust: SANCTIONED IMPORT-LANE PROOF-DROP (G6 reconciliation, 2026-08-23; count corrected 0 -> 1, see the G6 note below for why a correction is not a ratchet regression). fn Environment::add_decl, the `mm_axiom_only()` arm: an incoming Declaration::Theorem is converted to a Declaration::Axiom whose TYPE is registered WITHOUT infer_sort and whose proof value is dropped WITHOUT check_type. This is the Metamath two-pass importer's PASS-1, and it is the ONLY production (non-#[cfg(test)]) add_decl_unchecked / add_decl_structural dot-call in crates/**. SOUND because THREE independent in-tree mechanisms stand between it and any exported verdict - not because the flag is trusted. READ MECHANISM (3) IN FULL BEFORE QUOTING THIS ROW AS SETTLED: R1-MM (2026-08-27) REFUTED the sentence it rested on and REPAIRED it the same day, and one measurement on the shipped corpus is still outstanding. (1) FAIL-CLOSED ENTRY (Pillar-1 G1, 2026-07-01): the flag alone does not authorize the drop. The arm also requires mm_two_pass_active(), the thread-local sentinel only clean-olean's kernel_verify_two_pass_range establishes via the RAII MmAxiomOnlyGuard; a stray set_mm_axiom_only(true) anywhere else returns EnvError::AxiomOnlyMisuse instead of registering anything. The guard clears sentinel AND flag on drop (including a `?` early return), so the flag cannot leak into later checked work, and the thread-local default false keeps every other add_decl caller in the tree on the checked path. (2) PASS-2 RE-VERIFICATION: nothing pass-1 registers is ever a verification result - pass-1 leaves report.verified EMPTY. For each theorem in its range pass-2 forget_decl's the pass-1 axiom and re-adds it as a real Declaration::Theorem through the CHECKED add_decl, so that theorem's TYPE gets infer_sort and its PROOF gets check_type before it can be counted verified. Every exported theorem's type and proof were therefore kernel-checked. (3) DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE GATE - REFUTED 2026-08-27 (90aa719e4) AND REPAIRED THE SAME DAY (a2072b66a); READ THE WHOLE CLAUSE, INCLUDING THE OUTSTANDING MEASUREMENT, BEFORE RELYING ON IT. The mechanism: pass-2 checks a proof against an environment where OTHER theorems are still pass-1 axioms, so a theorem could type-check on an unproven dependency; crates/clean-olean/src/metamath/gate.rs (driven by crates/clean-olean/src/bin/mm_gate.rs) removes, to a fixpoint, every verified theorem whose transitive $p-dependency closure is not itself verified. WHAT STOOD HERE WAS FALSE. The sentence "the surviving set is exactly what the sequential verifier accepts" was refuted BY EXECUTION and pinned as a characterization test: over disjoint ranges 0..1 and 1..2, gate(two-pass) = {gth, usegth} while sequential = {gth} - a STRICT SUPERSET. CAUSE: the gate predicate is `D in verified` and carries no notion of WHICH TYPE D was checked against. Pass-1 (register_metamath_theorem_type_light) puts a theorem LIGHT SCHEMATIC type in the env and its label in cache/sigs UNCONDITIONALLY - including for a theorem whose real verification falls back to the GROUND (non-reusable) shape, which the sequential verifier lets nothing reuse. So a worker whose pass-2 range EXCLUDES that dependency verifies a dependent against the pass-1 type, and the gate KEEPS the dependent because the dependency genuinely is in `verified`. The divergence is PERMISSIVE, not fail-closed, and it was MASKED in the only configuration the original equivalence check ever ran (range = 0..max_provables, ONE worker over the whole prefix, every dependency re-verified in source order before its dependents); production (scripts/mm_two_pass.sh) splits into DISJOINT ranges. WHAT CLOSED IT (a2072b66a, entirely in crates/clean-olean - no kernel change, the pass-1 path above is untouched): every REAL verification now records its `reusable` bit in KernelVerifyReport::ground_only; mm_verify_range emits it as an ADDITIONAL `G <label>` line under a VERIFIED_FORMAT 2 stamp (the forked pass-2 child sink too, so the fact survives the parallel path); and the gate fixpoint now drops any theorem citing a dependency that is not KEPT and CITABLE. The ground-only theorem itself SURVIVES - sequential verifies it too, only CITATIONS of it are refused. FAIL-CLOSED ON THE MARKING is what makes the additive format safe: an UNSTAMPED labels file means reusability UNKNOWN, not nothing-was-ground-only, so mm_gate REFUSES it by default naming cause/risk/fix (--allow-unmarked proceeds with every unmarked label NON-citable, which can only under-approximate, never over-), and the driver stamps only if EVERY worker output carried it, so a stale mm_verify_range binary yields an unstamped union that the gate refuses. Equality with the sequential set is now MEASURED on four corpora in BOTH the full-range and the production split-range configurations, and the characterization test was INVERTED per its own doc rather than deleted (crates/clean-olean/tests/mm_two_pass_theorem.rs, test_ground_fallback_dep_no_longer_diverges_from_sequential). Only the gated set is exported - crates/clean-mathverse/src/bin/mm_export_verified.rs emits ONLY labels present in V, and the additive `G` line leaves every v1 reader byte-for-byte unaffected - so an unproven pass-1 axiom can appear neither as, nor beneath, a KernelVerified label. STILL OWED, AND THE REASON THIS ROW STAYS AT 1: the set.mm EXPOSURE measurement. The fix is in the code and machine-checked on synthetic corpora, but nobody has yet measured whether the ALREADY-SHIPPED mathverse Metamath export contains theorems the fixed gate now drops. The harness is BUILT and itself mechanized (so the number is a measurement, not an artifact of an untested detector), and the box that landed the fix has no Metamath corpus: on a corpus-bearing box, `mm_kverify <set.mm> <N> --exposure` runs the SEQUENTIAL verifier and prints every skip naming a dependency that IS in report.verified, then a verdict line. Exit 3 = measured EXPOSED (the shipped shard must be re-gated and re-exported, and the delta stated), 0 = measured CLEAN, 1/2 = the run broke - deliberately distinct, so a crash can never read as a clean bill of health. CLEAN would mean the equality held by accident of that corpus, NOT that the pre-fix argument was correct. Until that verdict is recorded, mechanism (3) is "repaired and measured on adversarial synthetic corpora, unmeasured on the shipped corpus" - it is not yet the unqualified claim this row once made. Full record, witness corpus and exit criteria: docs/issues/2026-08-23-r1-mm-two-pass-theorem.md (sections 3, 5, 6, 8, 8.5, 8.6). CONTAINMENT: pass-1 axioms live only in the importer's in-process Environment; they are never persisted, never re-exported, and carry no trust verdict (the Pass1Types export path is filtered to the already-verified wanted set). WHY IT IS NOT REMOVED: routing pass-1 through the checked path would not remove the deviation, it would HIDE it - pass-1 would still skip the proof, but as an ordinary axiom registration invisible to this ratchet - and it would re-run the applySubstV/MMThm reductions the light path exists to avoid (register_metamath_theorem_type_light). Counting it keeps the deviation named and pinned. SOUND AS TRUSTED CLOSURE CONTEXT (2026-07-08, gate green-up after the P4 per-constant-verify landing left 2 unaccounted sites): fn insert_or_upgrade demand-loads the transitive CONSTANT closure of a per-constant-verify target into the shared kernel environment (2 call sites: the stale-entry re-insert arm and the fresh-insert arm). Closure constants are imported CONTEXT, trusted exactly like the eager import closure `stamp-verified --closure-root` loads: they are never stamped KernelVerified, never certified, and never enter a trust receipt. Only the named TARGET constant(s) run the kernel's add_decl-equivalent check_type gauntlet, and only kernel-accepted targets become receipt leaves. A corrupt or wrong closure constant can at worst fail the target's kernel check (fail closed) - it cannot mint a false KernelVerified or widen any certified claim.
